_comment: Words whose relations ko.wiktionary files under the wrong part of speech.
`build_relations.py` scopes a page to the heading matching how this app
teaches the word, and that scoping is what stops 쪼다 the verb inheriting
쪼다 the insult's 유의어 바보, and 만세 the cheer inheriting 만세 the noun's
노년 · 늘그막 · 만년. Twenty-nine taught words have relations stated under a
heading other than their own, and twenty-five of them are that case: a
The four here are the other case. The word is the same word, the relations
are the ones a Korean speaker would give, and the wiki filed them under a
heading this app does not use for it. 밝다 is the clearest: the page's
*유의어: 환하다 / *반의어: 어둡다 sit in the 동사 block, whose sense is 해가
떠올라 날이 새다 — 'to dawn'. 밝다 as taught here is 빛이 많아 환하다, which
is the 형용사 block, and 어둡다 is its opposite in either reading.
Each entry names the heading to read instead, and says why. Nothing else
changes: the relation still has to be stated on the page, still has to be
mutual, and still has to point at a word this app ships. This file widens
*where the parser looks*, never what counts as a relation.
Adding to it should be rare and should always mean 'the wiki is wrong about
the part of speech', never 'I would like this pair to appear'.

밝다.heading: verb
밝다.why: the 형용사 block carries the taught sense and no relations; 환하다 and 어둡다 are stated in the 동사 block and hold for both readings

잘생기다.heading: verb
잘생기다.why: 표준국어대사전 files 잘생기다 as a verb and this app teaches it as an adjective; 못생기다 is its opposite either way

잘나다.heading: verb
잘나다.why: the same split as 잘생기다 — filed 동사 on the wiki, taught here as a description

신선하다.heading: verb
신선하다.why: a 하다 descriptive the wiki put under 동사; the taught sense is the one the block defines
